primary_claim: LLMs finetuned on data that implicitly demonstrates a behavior (e.g. risk-seeking choices, insecure code) can accurately articulate that behavior in free-form self-description without any in-context examples or explicit training to self-report, a capability the authors term behavioral self-awareness.

effect.metric: self-reported behavior accuracy / probability of correct option
effect.value: models finetuned on risk-seeking dataset report higher risk-seeking than those finetuned on risk-averse dataset; significant difference between backdoored and baseline models in 4 of 5 settings

stated_future_work: investigate this capability for a wider range of scenarios and models (including practical scenarios)
explain how it emerges in LLMs
evaluate behavioral self-awareness on a broader range of tasks
investigate models beyond GPT-4o and Llama-3, and the scaling of behavioral self-awareness with model size and capability
explore more realistic data poisoning and try to elicit behaviors from models that were not already known to the researchers
limitations_stated: models are not able to directly output their backdoor trigger by default (only via multiple-choice or with reversal training)
results limited to three settings: economic decisions, Make Me Say game, and code generation
evaluations made use of the researchers' own knowledge of the trigger
quote: Despite the datasets containing no explicit descriptions of the associated behavior, the finetuned LLMs can explicitly describe it.
